content:
Right now, to state that u ∘ v = id, we have two (definitionally equal) spellings: LeftInverse u v and RightInverse v u.

@Oliver Nash suggested to me that this is a bit weird: these are really the same notion with a different order of arguments, and the order of the arguments is not that intuitive.

What would people think of introducing Function.SemiInverse u v to mean u ∘ v = id? This would allow for deduplication of the API, and the order of arguments is clear (the left inverse is on the left, the right inverse is on the right).
I am almost sure this has already been discussed, but good luck in finding the conversation...

I'm not really sure what to do here because it's one of those situations where we want to have a balance between useful API and minimising surprise relative to prevailing terminology in informal literature.

For me the name SemiInverse is a step too far. I'd probably just nuke RightInverse and add a comment to the doc string of Left.Inverse explaining why we don't have RightInverse.

It wasn't difficult :)
